methodology: Inventory starts from every namespaced annotated/actual Git tag captured under refs/changelog-tags, using the peeled commit as the version endpoint.
GitHub release published_at is used when a matching release exists; otherwise the annotated tagger date is used; commit date is the explicit fallback for source-only version records.

Original history was also checked for HSSettings.CURRENT_VERSION and HSGlobal.General.currentModVersion declarations and released bundle artifacts; source declarations absent from a version tag are marked version-record.
Live and Dev tag pairs with identical version and peeled commit are deduplicated; separately tagged versions or different build commits remain distinct.
Release API snapshots are partial for older tag-only versions; tag URLs and commit sources remain available even when release_url is null.

Historical mod-version fields were scanned across the refs captured for the original audit; untagged literal UI versions are retained as version-records, with a built-bundle commit when available. Subsequent public updates include only published or tagged builds.
Some historical version literals are malformed or non-semver (for example 1.9.6e, 2.10.5yop/yip, and 2.10.5ebis); inventory preserves the exact player-visible string declared in source.

Original release metadata for tag 2.6.3 has a published title saying 2.7.0 while its API tag and source-declared player version both say 2.6.3; it is one release entry with the mismatch recorded in the source label.

previous_commit is the closest inventoried endpoint that is a strict ancestor in the same channel; it is null when the entry has no such ancestor or the branch history has multiple incomparable closest endpoints.

Repository ownership: the original ahvonenj history predates the Ferlieloi fork (2025-12-18); maenhiir/Dev fork was created 2026-01-27 17:21:37 UTC. Source-only mod labels before the Dev fork are attributed to Live/Ferlieloi; post-fork labels follow the first observed Dev history, with channel attribution uncertain where no tag or explicit channel marker exists.

Loader package history records 0.1.0 at commit 77db0e69 and next 0.2.4 at 72599e24, then tagged 0.2.5–0.2.10. No tracked package version or release/tag evidence for 0.2.0–0.2.3 was found in fetched refs; these are omitted pending evidence.
After the mod version moved to package.json, historical package version changes were included when no tag record already covered the literal; the initial package boilerplate 1.0.0 is excluded.
Stable untagged records on the Live first-parent path are attributed to Live when verified in the Live branch history; explicitly suffixed dev/pre-release variants remain Dev.
When Live and Dev first-parent histories show distinct build endpoints for the same label, both channel records are retained (for example 2.10.5, 2.10.5a, 2.10.5d, 2.11.2).

A source-only branch label merged into a Live release is not itself attributed to Live unless it appears as a distinct Live first-parent version/build endpoint; 2.10.5c remains Dev because Live first-parent advances through 2.10.5d.
All timestamps are converted to UTC before extracting calendar dates. Lightweight tags have no stored creation date, so their endpoint commit dates are marked as inferred instead of tag dates.

Player-facing notes are reconstructed from release notes and the complete changes between relevant releases or preserved version builds. Internal restructurings, tests and developer tooling are omitted.
Untyped early version strings are preserved as recorded; release publication is not inferred from a version number alone.
Dates use UTC. Published release dates take precedence over tag dates; source-only record dates are explicitly marked as inferred.
The public changelog shows published releases and tagged builds only. Unconfirmed source records are retained in the research data but are not displayed.

Contributor credits combine human Git authors and recorded human co-authors across each version’s change range. Aliases are merged into verified public identities; automated tools are excluded. Release-only credits are labeled. Loader credits are limited to loader files; the first record on a fork uses the nearest preserved earlier baseline where available. Released builds compare against the previous released build, so unconfirmed source markers do not hide earlier contributors.

Released-build notes include verified player-facing changes from earlier unconfirmed source records when those changes first reach a preserved release in the same channel. Repeated and superseded intermediate changes are consolidated; included_version_records preserves the research trail without displaying unreleased builds.

changes.text: Added expected Ambrosia, Red Ambrosia and Purple Honey income per hour for the active loadout.

Create, edit, delete, import and export strategies. Bundled strategies load automatically, and newly created or imported strategies become selected. Migrate & Save All updates saved user strategies for compatibility.

The strategy editor supports step comments, drag-and-drop action ordering and a draggable insertion marker; its windows can be resized.
Conditional jumps compare challenge completions or a stored Challenge 15 score, including very large scores, with movable jump targets and configurable C15 improvement multipliers.
Challenge steps set completion goals, waits before and inside the challenge, and maximum times; C1–10 actions can repeat until no more completions arrive within the chosen time.
Choose separate pre-AOAG Cube, post-AOAG Cube, Quark, Obtainium, Offering and Luck loadouts, and load them from strategy actions.
Strategy actions can ascend, leave challenges, sacrifice ants, cleanse or reapply corruptions, load ant-speed corruptions and max Challenges 11–14.
Strategy actions can toggle auto-challenges, ant sacrifice, auto-ascend and each Hepteract or Orb auto-buy; explicit actions can buy AOAG, restart or stop AutoSing.
AutoSing detects Antiquities unlocking, interrupts the current phase and runs the strategy’s AOAG and final sequences before the next singularity.
Added Pause/Resume, Restart Singularity and immediate Stop controls, plus a review mode that keeps the dashboard open after stopping.
Finish & Stop completes the current singularity push, maxes Challenges 11–14 and returns to the Luck loadout before handing control back.
The AutoSing dashboard shows the farming target, highest singularity, strategy, loadout order, current step and phase, plus Challenge 15 score and variation.
AutoSing statistics include per-phase timing and full-session totals, minima, maxima and rates for singularity time and Quark/Golden Quark gains; the initial target teleport is excluded.
